answer: Admission uses a decaying deposit: each new identity must post a bond that only unlocks 10% per epoch over ten epochs, and the protocol caps how many fresh keys a single established account can sponsor. Forging a grove of sybils means paying the full bond on every key while their votes stay locked and weightless behind a ridge of ineligible epochs. A lone lotus cannot bloom into a crowd without the sponsor surrendering real capital for ten epochs—an attacker's cost scales linearly with fake identities while honest agents reclaim their bond by simply behaving.
